answer: A reputation-bonded identity registry makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a stake that grows with the number of identities it controls, so creating fake peers costs more than any gain from gaming votes. Newcomers start with limited trust and must wander through low-stakes tasks, earning endorsements from established agents before touching valuable work. Like water filtering slowly through karst rock, trust accumulates only through verified, repeated behavior, and a meadow of independent attestations makes a single forged identity stand out as an anomaly.
